_comment: W15 — the demo's expected ranking, asserted. This file IS the demo: if it goes red,
the 90-second narrative on camera is wrong and no amount of good engineering rescues
Candidates are identified by resource, not by event id. The ids in `evidence_id` are
real auditIDs from `fixtures/k8s_audit/`, recorded from a live API server (W7b), and
they are asserted too — but as a provenance check, so that re-recording the fixture
fails loudly here rather than silently re-ranking a different set of events.
Scores are BANDS, not literals. A literal would make every legitimate weight tune a
test edit, which is how a golden test stops guarding anything. The bands are wide
enough to survive tuning inside Handoff §6's stated ranges and narrow enough that a
feature returning a constant falls out of them.

candidates.why: The causal change. Direct hit on the radius, 38 minutes before the alert, and Handoff §6's (update, configmap, connection-pool key) x latency_spike prior.
Direct hit, but 191 minutes back and no prior links a secret rotation to latency. Ranks second on temporal decay alone.
A one-hop dependency, so radius_overlap is 0.5 and it cannot reach rank 1 however recent it is. Out of band, like rank 1 — which is precisely why in_band must not be an input.
